what: numbers read directly off the box on 2026-09-21 for a fresh analysis of the last ten days; the ones marked unreported appear in no docs/*.md

1_presented_versus_never_presented.how: EVAL seats joined to SPLIT.json never_presented; medians over seats of SPECTRUM factor_relative, e_A, mu_max and the response-gate face median
1_presented_versus_never_presented.reading: box arms have NO generalisation gap (held-out equals presented at 0.03). Cut arms have a 2-7x gap AND a presented error already 4-9x the box arms'. Two problems at once: they do not fit, and what they fit does not transfer.

2_ncut_ladder_as_a_scaling_law.status: UNREPORTED as a law; NCUT_59 appears as one table row in CUT_CELL_ACCURACY_IS_ALL_CANCELLATION_20260919.md
2_ncut_ladder_as_a_scaling_law.fit: held-out error ~ n_seats^-0.21 between n=2 and n=59 (log(0.900/0.446)/log(59/2))
2_ncut_ladder_as_a_scaling_law.extrapolation: to reach 0.03 from 0.446 at n=59 needs n ~ 59 * (0.446/0.03)^(1/0.21) ~ 2.5e7 seats; even at an exponent of -0.5 it is ~1.3e4 seats, 40x the whole 296-cell pool
2_ncut_ladder_as_a_scaling_law.presented_error_RISES_with_seats: 0.033 -> 0.218 from 2 to 16 seats at 20k steps: the model cannot memorise more cut seats; 60k steps at 8 seats recovers 0.127 -> 0.048
2_ncut_ladder_as_a_scaling_law.reading: the observed data-scaling exponent makes the data route infeasible by three to five orders of magnitude. More geometries reduce memorisation and buy generalisation slowly; they cannot reach the contract.

3_where_the_error_sits_in_the_spectrum.how: mu = eig(R^-T A_hat R^-1); mu > 1 is predicted too stiff
3_where_the_error_sits_in_the_spectrum.reading: a box cell's error is a narrow band around 1; a cut cell's is heavy-tailed over seven orders of magnitude, in both directions. Even the memorised single seat keeps five directions 100x too stiff. This is the near-mechanism story made concrete: the network does not produce the cut cell's soft modes.

4_training_losses_and_convergence.reading: nothing has plateaued in training loss (every arm still falls 10-45 % per 10k steps), and the augmented dose arms sit 5x higher in-sample than the unaugmented. But the cut arm's operator error (e_factor) plateaued at 0.42 by 40k while its loss kept falling: the loss is being reduced on entries that do not carry the Frobenius error, i.e. the sampled block-pair loss does not weight the large soft-mode entries.

5_lattice_size_and_the_per_module_sensit.status: UNREPORTED: B444_100051 appears in docs only as a cost estimate (HANDOVER_20260920_0130.md:77), never as a result
5_lattice_size_and_the_per_module_sensit.reading: compliance stays inside contract at 64 cells (1.12 %) and the MEDIAN per-module sensitivity error is flat at ~1.1 %, but the TAIL widens: p90 goes 1.4-1.7 % at 2-8 cells to 4.8 % at 64, max to 9.1 %. p90 is a quantile, not a max statistic, so this is the distribution broadening, not more samples of the same one. Topology optimisation reads per-module sensitivities, so in a 64-cell lattice one module in ten gets a gradient off by more than 5 %, on the best-behaved seat. Sizes 2-8 are small samples; the 64-cell point is the only one with a real tail.

6_the_one_averaging_attempt_on_a_cut_cel.what_it_was: /root/_rank.sh: 'the free control: average the two single-seat cut models' M_q' = (NOAUG_100032 + SOLO_100032)/2 on seat 100032, then the two-cell self-glue
6_the_one_averaging_attempt_on_a_cut_cel.reading: this averaged the best single-seat model with the worst one (e_A 3.7 with e_A 1604) and came out 2.2x worse than the best alone. It is not the like-for-like two-model ensemble that bought the box cells a factor of two (ENSEMBLE_MW, whose 12 evaluation seats are all box). A proper ensemble on a cut cell has not been run.
